# MVPipeline — Crystal Structure Validation Pipeline

[![Python 3.x](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.x-blue.svg)](https://www.python.org/)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-yellow.svg)](https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT)

## About the Project

**MVPipeline** is a universal validator for CIF crystal structures generated by generative models: MatterGen, Con-CDVAE, CrystalFormer, and CrystalLLM.

Generative models can produce thousands of CIF files, but these often include:

- **Broken files** — the CIF cannot be parsed
- **Physically impossible structures** — atoms overlap or are too far apart from one another
- **Chemically incorrect structures** — the charge is not balanced
- **Duplicates** — the model repeatedly generates the same structure
- **Non-novel structures** — structures that were already present in the training set

MVPipeline automatically runs the full CIF set through a unified pipeline, filters out invalid structures, and collects generation-quality metrics. One run produces a complete report.

---

## Output of a Single Run

```
outputs/my_model/
├── validation_report.json     # Final report with metrics
├── all_structures.csv         # Full dataset for all structures
├── validated_structures/      # Structures that passed validation
└── rejected_structures/       # Rejected structures + reason
```

---

## Features

| Feature | Description |
|---|---|
| CIF reading | Recursive search and safe reading of all `.cif` files from a directory |
| Geometric validation | Checks minimum/maximum interatomic distances and volume per atom |
| Physical constraints | Checks allowed density range and maximum number of atoms in the cell |
| Charge check | Estimates charge neutrality using predefined oxidation states |
| Duplicate removal | Structural comparison using `StructureMatcher` |
| Novelty check | Comparison with `train_reference.csv` by formula and space group |
| Magnetic structures | Detection of transition metals and rare-earth elements |
| Metrics and report | Automatic generation of `validation_report.json` and `all_structures.csv` |
| Docker support | Execution in an isolated environment via Docker |

---

## Installation

### Via conda

```bash
conda env create -f environment.yml
conda activate mvpipeline
pip install -e .
```

### Via Docker

```bash
bash scripts/run_docker.sh
```

---

## Quick Start

### Via CLI

```bash
mvp \
  --input-dir samples/mattergen_cifs \
  --out-dir outputs/mattergen \
  --train-reference train_reference.csv \
  --thresholds config/thresholds.yaml
```

### CLI Arguments

| Argument | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `--input-dir` | Directory with source CIF files (recursive search) |
| `--out-dir` | Directory for saving results (default: `outputs/<model_name>`) |
| `--train-reference` | Path to a CSV with training-set structures (for calculating `novelty_ratio`) |
| `--thresholds` | Path to a YAML file with validation thresholds (default: built-in values) |
| `--model-name` | Model name for the report (default: the `input-dir` folder name) |
| `--pretty / --no-pretty` | Pretty-print the final report to the console (default: `--pretty`) |

> **Note:** if `--thresholds` or `--train-reference` are not provided, the pipeline will continue with a warning — `novelty_ratio` will not be calculated, and the thresholds will be taken from the built-in defaults.

### Via Web UI (Streamlit)

```bash
streamlit run src/ui/app.py
```

After launch, open in your browser:

```bash
http://localhost:8501
```

---

## Configuration

All validation thresholds are defined in `config/thresholds.yaml`.

### Geometry

```yaml
geometry:
  d_min_reject: 0.7       # Distance < 0.7 Å → rejection (overlap)
  d_max_suspicious: 1.2   # Distance 0.7–1.2 Å → warning (suspicious)
  vol_min: 8.0            # Minimum volume per atom (Å³)
  vol_max: 40.0           # Maximum volume per atom (Å³)
```

### Physical Properties

```yaml
physical_properties:
  min_density: 0.5        # Minimum density (g/cm³)
  max_density: 30.0       # Maximum density (g/cm³)
```

### System Limits

```yaml
system_limits:
  max_n_atoms: 500        # Maximum number of atoms in the cell
```

### Oxidation States

Used for checking charge neutrality. Defined as a list of allowed oxidation states for each element:

```yaml
oxidation_states:
  Fe: [2, 3]
  Ni: [2, 3]
  O:  [-2, -1]
  Ti: [2, 3, 4]
  # ... etc.
```

### Magnetic Elements

A structure is marked as magnetic (`is_magnetic = True`) if it contains at least one element from the list. By default, the list includes 3d/4d/5d transition metals and all rare-earth elements:

```yaml
magnetic_elements:
  # 3d transition metals
  - Ti, V, Cr, Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu, Zn
  # 4d/5d transition metals
  - Mo, Ru, Rh, Pd, Re, Os, Ir
  # Rare-earth elements (lanthanides)
  - Sc, Y, La, Ce, Pr, Nd, Pm, Sm, Eu, Gd, Tb, Dy, Ho, Er, Tm, Yb, Lu
```

---

## Input Data Format

### train_reference.csv

A CSV file with structures from the training set. Used for the novelty check.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `id` | str | Unique structure identifier |
| `reduced_formula` | str | Reduced chemical formula, for example `Fe2O3` |
| `spacegroup` | int/str | Space-group number or symbol (optional) |

Example:

```csv
id,reduced_formula,spacegroup
mp-1234,Fe2O3,167
mp-5678,NiO,225
```

---

## Output Data Format

### Example validation_report.json

```json
{
  "model_name": "mattergen",
  "n_total": 1000,
  "n_validated": 820,
  "n_rejected": 180,
  "validity_ratio": 0.82,
  "magnetic_ratio": 0.47,
  "novelty_ratio": 0.63,
  "duplicate_ratio": 0.12,
  "avg_density": 5.34,
  "avg_volume_per_atom": 13.2,
  "rejection_reasons": {
    "cif_parse_error": 10,
    "overlap": 95,
    "charge_imbalance": 50,
    "duplicate": 25
  }
}
```

| Metric | Description |
|---|---|
| `n_total` | Number of CIF files found in `input-dir` |
| `n_validated` | Number of structures that passed all checks |
| `n_rejected` | Number of rejected structures |
| `validity_ratio` | `n_validated / n_total` |
| `magnetic_ratio` | Fraction of valid structures containing magnetic elements |
| `novelty_ratio` | Fraction of valid structures that did not match `train_reference` |
| `duplicate_ratio` | Fraction of files rejected as duplicates (relative to `n_total`) |
| `avg_density` | Average density of valid structures (g/cm³) |
| `avg_volume_per_atom` | Average volume per atom of valid structures (Å³) |
| `rejection_reasons` | Counter by rejection reason |

### all_structures.csv

Full dataset for all CIF files, intended for further analysis and model comparison.

| Field | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `structure_id` | str | Relative path to the CIF inside `input-dir` |
| `input_path` | str | Full path to the source CIF |
| `status` | str | `validated` or `rejected` |
| `rejection_reason` | str/null | Rejection reason |
| `is_suspicious` | bool | Soft-anomaly flag (distance in the 0.7–1.2 Å range) |
| `is_duplicate` | bool | Whether the structure is a structural duplicate |
| `is_novel` | bool | Whether the structure is novel relative to `train_reference` |
| `is_magnetic` | bool | Whether the structure contains magnetic elements |
| `n_atoms` | int | Number of atoms in the cell |
| `density` | float | Density (g/cm³) |
| `volume_per_atom` | float | Volume per atom (Å³) |
| `min_distance` | float | Minimum interatomic distance (Å) |
| `reduced_formula` | str | Reduced chemical formula |
| `spacegroup` | str/int/null | Space group |
| `charge_solution_json` | str/null | JSON with oxidation states |
| `details_json` | str | Full JSON with details for all checks |

### rejected_structures/

A `*.reason.json` file is created next to each rejected CIF:

```json
{
  "structure_id": "subdir/a.cif",
  "reason": "overlap",
  "details": {
    "min_distance": 0.42
  }
}
```

Rejection reason codes:

| Code | Description |
|---|---|
| `cif_parse_error` | The file cannot be parsed |
| `overlap` | Distance between atoms is below `d_min_reject` (0.7 Å) |
| `charge_imbalance` | The unit-cell charge is not neutral |
| `duplicate` | Structural duplicate of an already accepted structure |
| `density_out_of_range` | Density outside the `[min_density, max_density]` range |
| `volume_out_of_range` | Volume per atom outside the `[vol_min, vol_max]` range |
| `too_many_atoms` | Number of atoms exceeds `max_n_atoms` |

---

## How the Pipeline Works

```
Input directory with CIF files
    │
    ▼
1. CIF-file search
   Recursive traversal of input-dir and collection of all *.cif files
    │
    ▼
2. Loading train_reference
   Building a (formula, spacegroup) index for novelty checking
    │
    ▼
3. Processing each CIF:
    │
    ├─► CIF reading (pymatgen)
    │         └─ error → cif_parse_error → rejected
    │
    ├─► Sanity check
    │   Structure is not empty, lattice is correct, coordinates are valid
    │
    ├─► Geometric check
    │   Interatomic distances, volume per atom
    │         └─ distance < 0.7 Å → overlap → rejected
    │         └─ distance 0.7–1.2 Å → suspicious (warning)
    │         └─ volume outside [8.0, 40.0] Å³ → rejected
    │
    ├─► Physical-property check
    │   Density, number of atoms
    │         └─ density outside [0.5, 30.0] g/cm³ → rejected
    │         └─ number of atoms > 500 → rejected
    │
    ├─► Charge-neutrality check
    │   Estimation of oxidation states using the table from the config
    │         └─ non-zero charge → charge_imbalance → rejected
    │
    ├─► Descriptor calculation
    │   Density, volume per atom, formula, space group
    │
    ├─► Magneticity detection
    │   Checking for the presence of elements from magnetic_elements
    │   (metric, not a rejection reason)
    │
    ├─► Duplicate check
    │   StructureMatcher compares with already accepted structures
    │         └─ match found → duplicate → rejected
    │
    └─► Novelty check
        Comparison of (formula, spacegroup) with train_reference
        (metric, not a rejection reason)
    │
    ▼
4. Saving results
   Valid       → validated_structures/
   Rejected    → rejected_structures/ + *.reason.json
    │
    ▼
5. Building final artifacts
   all_structures.csv + validation_report.json
```

### Novelty Check

A structure is considered **not novel** if `train_reference.csv` already contains a record with the same `(reduced_formula, spacegroup)` pair. This makes it possible to quickly identify whether the model is producing obvious repetitions from the training set. Novelty is a **metric**, not a rejection reason.

### Duplicate Removal

Duplicates are identified structurally using `pymatgen.analysis.structure_matcher.StructureMatcher`, not by textual CIF comparison. Candidates are first grouped into buckets (formula / number of atoms / spacegroup) to avoid full pairwise comparison.

## Technologies

| Library | Purpose |
|---|---|
| [pymatgen](https://pymatgen.org/) | CIF reading, structural-property calculation, `StructureMatcher` |
| [spglib](https://spglib.readthedocs.io/) | Space-group symmetry determination |
| [typer](https://typer.tiangolo.com/) | CLI interface |
| [pandas](https://pandas.pydata.org/) | Reading `train_reference.csv`, creating `all_structures.csv` |
| [numpy](https://numpy.org/) | Numerical operations, metric aggregation |
| [tqdm](https://tqdm.github.io/) | Progress bar for processing thousands of files |
| [rich](https://rich.readthedocs.io/) | Readable logs and final console summary |
| Docker | Isolated pipeline execution |

---

## Scripts

| Script | Description |
|---|---|
| `scripts/run_validation.sh` | Run validation for multiple models in sequence |
| `scripts/run_docker.sh` | Run validation inside Docker |

---

## Model Comparison

After running the pipeline for different models, you can compare metrics from `validation_report.json`:

```bash
# MatterGen
mvp --input-dir samples/mattergen --out-dir outputs/mattergen ...

# Con-CDVAE
mvp --input-dir samples/cdvae --out-dir outputs/cdvae ...

# CrystalFormer
mvp --input-dir samples/crystalformer --out-dir outputs/crystalformer ...

# CrystalLLM
mvp --input-dir samples/crystallm --out-dir outputs/crystallm ...
```

Then compare `validity_ratio`, `novelty_ratio`, `duplicate_ratio`, `avg_density`, and other metrics across models for an objective evaluation of generation quality.
